# Rapier JXL

> JPEG XL encoder. ES modules. MIT. No runtime dependencies or automatic filesystem/network I/O.

Package: rapier-jxl
Version: 2.6.0
Install: npm install rapier-jxl
Pixel input: Uint8Array/Uint8ClampedArray (8-bit), Uint16Array (10/12/16-bit integers or raw binary16), Float32Array (binary32); width * height * 4 RGBA samples, row-major.
Pixel output: Uint8Array, bare JPEG XL codestream, extension .jxl, MIME image/jxl.
Execution: synchronous; browser, module worker, Node, Deno.
Core payload: 26,997 minified bytes; 11,408 gzip bytes.

## Entry selection

- rapier-jxl or rapier-jxl/core: encode(data, width, height, options?), encodeSteps, LIMITS. quality 100 by default; 1–99 lossy. Alpha exact. No bundled WebAssembly.
- rapier-jxl/effort: core capabilities plus effort 1–9, default 1; optional treeLearning: 'sampled'. Lossless candidates compete by complete byte length.
- rapier-jxl/wasm: effort API with inlined integer kernels; automatic SIMD or JavaScript; same output bytes. Also configureKernels and kernelMode.
- rapier-jxl/jpeg: transcode(jpegBytes, options?), transcodeSteps, LIMITS. Returns {bytes, width, height, orientation}; keeps coefficients, orientation and an admitted colour-space declaration; omits reconstruction data and other metadata.
- rapier-jxl/photo: encodePhoto(data, width, height, options?), encodePhotoSteps, LIMITS. Ordinary byte inputs use VarDCT below quality 100; native inputs use the shared modular path. Quality 90 by default, 100 lossless.
- rapier-jxl/jpeg-ans and rapier-jxl/photo-ans: corresponding JPEG/photo API; ANS search at effort 2 and above.
- Append /min to each named encoding import for its self-contained file. rapier-jxl/min is the minified core.
- rapier-jxl/writer: typed format primitives, readable source only. rapier-jxl/kernels: shared readable-module kernel controls.
- rapier-jxl/source: async readSource(Uint8Array | ArrayBuffer), PNG16 or supported scanline OpenEXR -> {data,width,height,bitDepth,sampleFormat,colorSpace,transferFunction,alphaPremultiplied,intensityTarget?}. Optional, no /min export.

## Contracts

- quality: number 1–100; lossless is quality: 100. Pixel primaries: colorSpace: 'srgb' (default), 'display-p3' or 'rec2020'; declaration, no sample conversion.
- bitDepth: 8 for bytes; Uint16Array integer code values use 10, 12 or 16 (default 16), never silently truncate. sampleFormat: 'float16' for raw half words; Float32Array infers 'float32'. Float formats fix bit depth at 16/32 and exponent width at 5/8.
- transferFunction: 'srgb', 'linear', 'pq', 'hlg'; integer default srgb, float default linear. intensityTarget defaults to 10000 nits for PQ, 1000 for HLG, otherwise 255; stored as binary16. No tone mapping or HDR clipping.
- alphaPremultiplied: boolean, default false; associated RGB remains associated, with no division. Source EXR with A sets true; PNG sets false. Alpha words stay exact at every quality.
- Native lossless uses the shared modular group planner. Efforts 2–9 also price untransformed integer RGB; floats have no extra lossless rung. Native lossy rounds RGB source code values/mantissas before reversible coding; a smaller exact candidate may win. See API for numeric error bounds and decoder qualifications.
- PNG16: all row filters, Adam7, gray/RGB with optional alpha, tRNS, supported cICP/sRGB/linear-gamma metadata. EXR: flat single-part scanlines, uniform HALF/FLOAT RGB or Y plus optional A, NONE/RLE/ZIPS/ZIP, square pixels, matching data/display windows. Unsupported profiles/layouts require another reader; no archival metadata round trip.
- effort: integer 1–9, default 1; supported by effort, wasm, JPEG and photo entries. Core has no effort option.
- Limits: 16 MiB output, 16,384 pixels per side. Core/effort/wasm: 24 million pixels. Photo: 40 million. JPEG: 64 million and 16 MiB input.
- Checked encoding entry error codes: JXL_INPUT, JXL_DIMENSIONS, JXL_SIZE, JXL_MEMORY, JXL_JPEG. Inspect error.code; diagnostic text is not the contract. Raw writer primitives have unchecked preconditions.
- Jobs yield progress in (0, 1]. Read job.bytes only after iteration completes. Leaving the loop cancels; job.hurry requests a completed candidate. Sampled lossless hurry returns effort 1 exactly.
- Output is deterministic: the same pixels and options write the same bytes in every JavaScript engine, with or without the WebAssembly kernels.
- Search candidates stop only when their completed section bytes already reach the retained complete stream size. Pruning does not signal hurry or cancel later candidates.
- Input stays unmodified and must remain available until completion or cancellation. Input buffer transfer detaches it from the sender.
- A carried JPEG cannot reconstruct the original JPEG file. Unsupported or malformed JPEGs raise JXL_JPEG; decode and encode pixels when appropriate.
